mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months indicates a shift toward monetary easing, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of 20-day windows following easing signals, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% triggers a sudden tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing the present value of expected equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in > 80% of tightening windows, or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 150,000 over 3 consecutive months signals weakening labor market demand, lowering consumer confidence and corporate investment, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of such labor weakness windows, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) below 120,000 for 3 consecutive months indicates improving labor market conditions, raising consumer and business confidence and corporate investment, thereby producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day forward returns in > 80% of recovery windows, or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (GDPC1) exceeding 2% for 3 consecutive months indicates robust consumer demand, prompting companies to raise guidance and expand capital expenditures, thereby producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of strong-demand windows, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 1% for 3 consecutive months signals supply-side constraints, reducing corporate earnings visibility and consumer confidence, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in > 80% of contraction windows, or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for 3 consecutive months indicates a strengthening labor market, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain or cut rates, lowering discount rates and boosting equity valuations, thereby producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of strengthening windows, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,200,000 for 3 consecutive months indicates a cooling housing market, reducing consumer wealth and corporate earnings visibility, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in > 80% of cooling windows, or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
